summary: SSE stream drops intermediate sentence during mobile network handoff (Wi‑Fi→Cellular)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when a mobile client switches networks mid-stream (Wi‑Fi → Cellular) the SSE session reconnect completes, but the stream restarts from a later token and an entire intermediate sentence is dropped. The resumed stream includes tokens that make the final output syntactically correct but missing a whole clause from the middle of the response.

Impact:
- Affects a small subset of enterprise customers using long streaming responses on mobile apps.
- User-visible missing sentences in generated content (integrated note-taking app) leading to content correctness issues.
- Occurs intermittently during network handoffs; not blocking but causes unacceptable data loss for the customer (enterprise tier SLA).

Environment:
- Prod, us-east region behind our CDN + cloud LB (customer uses iOS app 16.x and Android 13).
- Client uses EventSource (SSE) via our JS shim (redwood-client-js v1.4.2) with automatic reconnect.
- Typical responses: 800–1200 tokens.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start a streaming SSE generation from the app with a long prompt (expected >600 tokens).
2. While stream is active on Wi‑Fi, toggle device to airplane mode briefly then re-enable (or force switch to cellular).
3. Observe that client reconnects and receives a resumed stream but the middle sentence of the earlier content is missing.

Observed logs (selected):
- Gateway: [2026-03-05T13:22:17Z] conn=abcd1234 handoff detected, upstream=cdn-edge-7 GOAWAY
- Edge: [2026-03-05T13:22:17Z] session_token=st-98765 swapped -> st-98765-2, mapping_lookup OK
- Serving: [2026-03-05T13:22:17Z] resume_offset=11234, kv_cache_validation=FAIL (expected_prefix_hash!=observed)
- Client SDK: reconnect eventId=evt-3105, last_received_offset=11102

Notes: the delta between last_received_offset (client) and resume_offset (server) maps to ~1 sentence (≈150 tokens) and kv_cache_validation returned FAIL which triggers the runtime to fast-forward to a safe continuation point; that fast-forward point is after the missing sentence.

Attachments:
- HAR and EventSource logs supplied by customer (attached in ticket)
- CDN and LB traces were linked in comments below.

Desired outcome:
- On network handoff/reconnect, resume behavior must preserve all previously delivered tokens or deliver a clear overlap/deduplication so no content is silently lost.
comments: Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-05: Acknowledged receipt; asked customer for HAR and SDK logs and whether they were using our official client. Also requested a short repro prompt that reliably produces the missing sentence.

Customer (Emily Park, Noteable Labs) 2026-03-05: Uploaded HAR and EventSource logs, confirmed official redwood-client-js v1.4.2. Provided repro prompt and timeline (Wi‑Fi→Cellular). Reports ~30% reproducibility on short handoff (<2s).

SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-06: Found LB GOAWAY during handoff and session_token rotation in edge logs. Noted KV cache validation failures at serving runtime correlated to those timestamps. Tentatively suspect token-to-session mapping race.

Eng (Rina Patel) 2026-03-07: Reproduced locally with simulated CDN handoff. Confirmed scenario: when session token is rotated during socket migration the resume_offset calculation can pick a conservative continuation index leading to skipping an intermediate sentence. Submitted preliminary PR to improve offset alignment.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-09: Informed customer of ongoing investigation and provided a temporary client-side mitigation (buffer last 2 SSE events and apply simple dedupe by eventId on reconnect).
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced with local proxy that injects GOAWAY then re-establishes connection with new session token.
- Root cause appears to be a race: edge rotates session token and clears short-term mapping before serving confirms KV cache prime; when serving receives a reconnect it fails kv_cache_validation and uses resume_offset computed from model token checkpoints which rounds up to the next choice boundary.
- The rounding logic was intentionally conservative to avoid duplicating tokens but in this case skips a mid-sentence chunk.
- The client reported last_received_offset was accurate; mismatch arises because edge reported a different token base after rebind.
- Affected code paths: edge token swap handler, session id mapping TTL (10s), serving runtime resume offset snap-to-boundary logic.
resolution:
Workaround deployed (2026-03-10): increased session mapping TTL to 30s on edge and added a short 'hold-and-verify' step that attempts to validate observed client offset against KV cache before fast-forwarding. This reduced occurrences in canary from ~30% -> ~2%.
Planned fix: engineering PR github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 modifies resume logic to compute minimal overlapping window and prefer overlap + dedupe rather than fast-forward. Edge PR github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/421 prevents premature mapping eviction on token rotation. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-15 with feature flag.
root_cause: Race between edge session-token rotation and serving-runtime KV cache validation. Resume logic preferred fast-forward to safe boundary when validation failed, which skipped an intermediate sentence during network handoff.
next_steps:
1) Deploy edge PR to all prod edge nodes behind feature flag and monitor metrics (duplication and missing-chunk rate).
2) Merge runtime PR and enable minimal-overlap resume logic; ensure unit tests for sentence-boundary cases.
3) Add telemetry to capture resume_offset vs client_last_offset deltas and alert if >50 tokens.
4) Customer follow-up: schedule call to validate rollout with Noteable Labs after full deployment.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation in prod; final fix targeted for 2026-03-15
